summary:
A hard first Christmas after a loss is often part of typical grief. A study of older widowed adults found distress was higher around a late partner's birthday and in January after the holidays, in the early months after a loss. Prolonged grief is different: longing that stays intense for many months and makes daily life hard to manage.

Our new article from psychologist Matthew Hallam explains the difference, and when it may be worth talking to your GP.

Equal Psychology provides psychological support for adults experiencing grief and loss in Kew, Croydon, and online across Melbourne.

If this time of year is bringing up something difficult, Lifeline is available on 13 11 14.

Medicare rebates available with a GP referral.

Read more: https://equalpsychology.com.au/blog/grief-at-christmas-prolonged-grief
